### Observed differences

- A01 appears only in the later window: it is absent from all 200 earlier traces, but occurs in about 95 of 200 traces (about 48 in 100) afterwards, exactly once per trace when present. [OCC001]
- In the later window A01 sits late in the trace: its median position is about 0.85 of the trace length, and about a quarter of its occurrences are the trace's final event. [POS001]
- A18's outgoing transitions changed from a spread over about ten activities (largest about 19% to A10, about 13% each to A06 and A12, with A01 never a successor) to a strong focus on A01: about 65 in 100 of A18's outgoing transitions now lead to A01. [DIR004]
- The A01–A18 relationship changed from never co-occurring to always co-occurring in a fixed order: earlier, A18 appeared without A01 in about 40 in 100 traces and A01 never appeared; later, both occur together in about 48 in 100 traces, always with A18 before A01, and A18 no longer occurs without A01. [REL001]
- A01's own outgoing transitions, observable only in the later window, spread over about ten activities (about 17% to A10, 15% to A07, 14% to A12) — a set closely resembling A18's earlier successor set. [DIR001]
- Repetition shifted between two existing activities: A02's mean occurrences per trace rose from about 0.48 to about 1.01 (participation roughly stable at 48–54%) and it now recurs in about 26 in 100 traces, while A08's mean fell from about 0.87 to about 0.48 and it no longer recurs (previously about 20 in 100), at unchanged participation of about 47 in 100 traces. [OCC002, OCC003]
- Outgoing shares at two further activities redistributed: A09 now leads to A02 in about 65 in 100 of its transitions (previously about 38; A07, previously about 17%, is no longer observed), and A14 leads to A08 in about 24 in 100 (previously about 63), with A15 newly observed at about 19% and A06 up to about 21%. [DIR002, DIR003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that A01 was inserted as a new late-stage step executing after A18. In the earlier window A01 was not observed at all; in the later window it occurs in about 48 in 100 traces, always after A18 and typically near the end of the trace, while A18 — which previously distributed its outgoing transitions over many activities — now leads to A01 in about 65 in 100 of them, and A01's own successor set mirrors what A18 previously pointed to. This placement is shown directly by relational and positional evidence rather than inferred from frequency shifts. [OCC001, POS001, REL001, DIR004, DIR001]

The screening context makes a chance reading of the overall pattern implausible: 9 items qualified from 40 tested units where only about 0.2 would be expected if nothing had changed. Limitations: the five A01-related items largely describe one underlying difference rather than independent confirmations, and the evidence establishes that A01 was unobserved earlier, not why — a recording or sampling gap in the earlier window cannot be fully excluded, although 0 of 200 traces versus 95 of 200 makes pure sampling fluctuation unlikely. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, POS001, REL001]

Other differences: A02 now repeats (mean about 0.48 to about 1.01 occurrences per trace, recurrence from 0 to about 26 in 100) while A08 no longer does (mean about 0.87 to about 0.48, recurrence from about 20 to 0 in 100); outgoing shares at A09 shifted toward A02 and at A14 away from A08 toward A15 and A06. No relational evidence ties these to the A01 insertion, so they may be separate changes. [OCC002, OCC003, DIR002, DIR003]

An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the repetition and routing changes reflect an independent modification (for example, rework moving between A08 and A02) rather than consequences of the A01 insertion, since no relational items link them; the evidence also cannot distinguish a genuine process addition from a difference in how the two windows were recorded. [OCC002, OCC003, DIR002, DIR003]
